chunks: From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazal, from Al-Hasan ibn Jahm who said:

I heard Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) saying: 'The dream is upon what interpretation you give it.' So I said to him: 'Some of our companions reported that the dream of the king was a confused dream.' So Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said: 'A woman saw a dream during the time of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) that the pillar of her house had broken. So she came to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and related the dream to him. The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said to her: 'Your husband will come to you safely.' And her husband had been absent, so he came just as the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said. Then her husband went away for another time. She saw in her sleep as if the pillar of her house had broken. So she came to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and related the dream to him. So he (peace be upon him and his family) said to her: 'Your husband will come to you safely.' So he came as he (peace be upon him and his family) had said. Then her husband went away for a third time. She saw in her sleep that the pillar of her house had broken. She met a left-handed man, so she related the dream to him. The bad man said to her: 'Your husband is dead.' He said: 'So that reached the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), so he (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'If only he had interpreted it for her in a good way.'.
ai.seo_question: How does the interpretation of a dream affect its reality according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the Shia concept of *ta'bir* (interpretation) as a creative act that can influence reality, contrasting the Prophet’s authoritative, positive interpretation with the fatalistic view of a fortune teller. It underscores the spiritual power of the Imams and the Prophet in shaping outcomes through their words, a principle rooted in the Quranic narrative of Joseph. The narrative serves as a practical demonstration of how divine insight can alter destiny, reinforcing the status of the Ahl al-Bayt as true interpreters of signs.
